user.title: Guest panel
user.description: A page at `/guest` for people visiting your home: no account, no app. It only answers devices connected to the networks you list.

data_description.networks: Your Wi-Fi network in CIDR format, for example 192.168.1.0/24. You can add several.

error.invalid_network: One of the networks is not valid. Use the format 192.168.1.0/24.

panel.title: Guest panel
panel.description: A page at `/guest` for people visiting your home: no account, no app. It only answers devices connected to the networks you list.

data_description.networks: Your Wi-Fi network in CIDR format, for example 192.168.1.0/24. You can add several.

add_user.title: Restrict a user
add_user.description: Pick a Home Assistant user who is not an administrator. They will stop seeing and controlling everything you do not allow in the next step.

data.condition_entity: Entity that shows they are home

data_description.always_entities: They can see and control these from anywhere.
data_description.family_location: Always allows the map (people and zones) and the Family Location entities, including the check-in and ask-for-help buttons.
data_description.home_entities: They can see and control these only while the condition below is met.
data_description.condition_entity: Usually the Wi-Fi connection sensor of their phone (Home Assistant app). A device_tracker from your router also works.
data_description.condition_states: Your Wi-Fi name (SSID), exactly as the sensor shows it. For a device_tracker, type home.
data_description.away_read: If off, these entities do not appear to them while away.

remove_user.title: Stop restricting
remove_user.description: The users you pick get the normal access of a Home Assistant user back.

error.invalid_network: One of the networks is not valid. Use the format 192.168.1.0/24.

abort.no_users: There are no users to restrict. First create a non-administrator user in Settings → People.
